title: MBC to Air LCK Finals Through 2027 After 0.4% Debut Rating
summary: MBC to Air LCK Finals Through 2027 After 0.4% Debut Rating  The Esports Advocate
content:
LCK Trophy. Image credit: Riot Games Korea

Riot Games has extended its broadcast agreement with MBC to carry the League of Legends Champions Korea Finals live on South Korean terrestrial television through 2027, taking the country’s premierLeague of Legendscompetition to a third consecutive year on national TV.

According toRiot Games’ announcement Thursday, the two-year contract covers the 2026 and 2027 Finals. This year’s final takes place Sept. 13 at 2 p.m. KST at the KSPO Dome in Olympic Park in Seoul’s Songpa district, with the finals qualifier at the same venue the day before. MBC has again placed the match in the Sunday afternoon slot it uses for professional baseball and other major sports, and said it would assemble a commentary team aimed at viewers new to the league and trail the event through its sports news bulletins.

Financial terms were not disclosed. Neither the 2025 nor the 2026 agreement has established whether MBC pays a rights fee, co-produces the broadcast with Riot Games, or carries it on a revenue-sharing or barter basis.

The renewal follows a debut broadcast that drew a modest audience.

MBC’s live coverage of the 2025 final — in which Gen.Gdefeated Hanwha Life Esports 3-1at Inspire Arena in Incheon on Sept. 28 — recorded a 0.4% nationwide household rating, according to Nielsen Korea figuresreported by Daily Esports. Seoul and Daejeon returned 0.7%, the wider capital region 0.5%, and Busan and Gwangju 0.2%. MBC’s own News Desk drew 5.8% the same evening, and a concurrent KBO League game on SBS drew 0.7%. The final did not feature T1, the league’s most internationally followed team, whose elimination the outlet reported had already raised concerns about the audience the broadcast would deliver.

title: League of Legends champion DRX sets sights beyond gaming
summary: League of Legends champion DRX sets sights beyond gaming  The Korea Herald
content:
Two TV shows, mobile games, Southeast Asian expansion anchor broader entertainment push

DRX, the Korean esports organization behind the 2022 League of Legends World Championship run that popularized the phrase “unbreakable spirit,” is setting its sights beyond gaming.

Korean shows backed by its subsidiary are set to debut in the fourth quarter, marking the first major step in DRX’s bid to become an entertainment group, said CEO Yang Sun-il.

“The boundaries between content such as games, K-dramas and films have already collapsed,” Yang said in an interview with The Korea Herald at the company’s headquarters in Seoul on Wednesday.

"They are all ultimately part of the entertainment business. What differs is simply how they give people enjoyment.”

Yang highlighted two examples: Blizzard turned World of Warcraft, one of the world's most successful massively multiplayer online role-playing games, or MMORPGs, into a theatrical feature film; Tencent and Smilegate produced a popular Chinese series based on the latter’s shooting game Crossfire, which was a megahit in China.

title: 4v4 arrives to Compete TFT
content:
Yes, you read that right. The 4v4 format is coming back and it’s open to all players in AMER, EMEA, and APAC. Tactician’s Superbrawl is a team tournament running November 6th to 8th. EMEA players might remember the name from Rising Legends, where Superbrawl ran as a community event. This time it's part of our official esports circuit!

Built for players looking to join the official competitive ecosystem, the tournament will offer qualification opportunities for Set 19 Tactician's Trials. All four members of a winning team earn their spot, though Trials is always played solo, so there's no 4v4 format there. TPC players may be drafted onto teams, with a maximum of two per roster, but they are not eligible to qualify for Set 19 Tactician's Trials through this event.

Players that compete in Tactician’s Trials have been telling us the season ends too early, and they're right. Tactician’s Superbrawl extends it by around three weeks and gives late season ladder play something concrete to aim at, whether you started grinding in August or picked things up in October. November has something on it now.

It's also a format the community has been playing on its own for a long time. Bringing 4v4 into official competition recognizes that, and it adds a competitive space that works differently from anything else on the calendar. You pick your teammates, you represent your region, and you build something together in this new format.

Tactician’s Superbrawl will consist of96 teams per regioncompeting in a single elimination best-of-3 bracket. Players can qualify in two ways:

To earn acaptain slot, finish at the top of your server’s snapshot. Captains will then draft three teammates from the eligible pool, which runs a lot deeper into the ladder than the captain slots do. TPC players are eligible to be drafted assuming they answer your messages... Two per team, maximum.
